This is the suggested style for the figures in MAR2. We would be glad if you followed it wherever you can: a report whose graphics are consistent within each chapter and across all of them reads as one piece, and carries more weight.

Above all, aim for figures that are not only clear but also beautiful. Readers notice, and they spend more time with a figure that is a pleasure to look at. The more time they spend, the better they understand it; the better they understand it, the more likely they are to reuse it and share it. And every time a figure is shared, the report’s findings travel a little further.

Colour

Blue and red are the report’s main colours. We’ll use blue within the figures, but mostly for text across the report. The palettes below are for data, and a figure takes one of them for its subject.

Blue, responses and action#2B3178
Red, risk and impact#B3402B

Below are a few examples of colour palettes we encourage you to use. The full Scientific Colour Maps library holds many more, and each palette can be downloaded in formats for direct use in QGIS, MATLAB, R, Python and others.

Sea, water, marine, coastal
Land, vegetation, soil, agriculture
People, society, health, economy
Change, anomaly, gain and loss

Fonts

The font we would like to use across the report is Open Sans. It is free and open-licensed, so nobody has to buy anything — download it from Google Fonts. Regular, SemiBold and Bold are the only weights used.

TitleOpen Sans Bold, 12 pt
DeckOpen Sans Regular, 8 pt
Panel labelOpen Sans Bold, 9 pt
LabelOpen Sans SemiBold, 6 pt
AnnotationOpen Sans Regular, 7 pt

Title and deck

We would like every figure to open with a title and a deck. Title is the main finding, as a sentence. Title has no full stop at the end. Deck says what we are looking at, in an ordinary descriptive sentence rather than a technical string, and it ends with a full stop.

Example:

Forest area grew in every subregion

Forest cover during 1990–2020 across three Mediterranean subregions.

Panel labels

Where a figure has panels, we suggest labelling them like this: a lower case letter and a full stop.

Example:

a.Forest area.

b.Annual rate of change.

Maps

This is the suggested map projection for the Mediterranean region. Lambert Conformal Conic at standard parallels 33° N and 45° N, central meridian 15° E, on WGS84 — it's also the typical projection in IPCC reports.

+proj=lcc +lat_1=33 +lat_2=45 +lat_0=39 +lon_0=15 +datum=WGS84 +units=m

Delivery format

Where you can, please send figures in an editable format: a vector file with the fonts embedded, so type, colour and labelling can be brought into the report style without anything being redrawn. PDF, AI and EPS carry their fonts with them; an SVG does not, so if SVG is easiest for you, please send the font file alongside it, or let us know which font you used.

If a figure can only be shared as a flat image, 300 dpi at the final printed size would help.

Size500 pt maximum width (176 mm), at the size the figure will be printed
PreferredVector, with the fonts embedded — PDF, AI or EPS
OtherwiseA flat image at 300 dpi
